title: worktree merge: a missing lane record must not let cleanup delete the worktree under uat_stop close
action: A narrow hole the semantic judge found in usp-2 (verdict PASS, observation 1) — it passes the letter of usp-2's truths and defeats their purpose, so it is fixed rather than filed. Under uat_stop close, set_lane_uat_wait_on_merge returns early with uat_wait_set false when the feature has a live workflow record but NO .bee/lanes/<feature>.json on disk. merge_finish then computes effective_cleanup as cleanup AND NOT uat_wait_set, so cleanup is NOT suppressed and the worktree is torn down — taking away the only place a failed uat can be fixed, and dropping the grant so the second merge cannot even run. The two branches are asymmetric: the merge-time precondition fails CLOSED in the same situation, because uat_gate_applies_to_lane(None) returns true. FIX: make the cleanup suppression fail closed the same way the precondition already does. Under uat_stop close, when the feature's uat is unapproved and the lane rule says the lane cares (including the fails-closed-as-standard case of a missing or unrecognized classification), cleanup is suppressed REGARDLESS of whether the lane file could be written. Whether the lane record exists is a bookkeeping fact; whether the user still needs their worktree is not, and the second must not be decided by the first. Keep every other behavior exactly as usp-2 left it: the lane write itself stays best-effort warn-never-fail (a missing lane record still must not turn a green merge red, and still must not fabricate a lane file), the Merge and Off branches are untouched, and --no-cleanup still means keep. Name the suppression the same way usp-2 does so the reported result key stays consistent. Tests in worktree/tests.rs: under uat_stop close with uat unapproved and NO lane record on disk, a merge with --cleanup keeps the worktree, keeps the branch, and keeps the grant, and the same merge reports the cleanup suppression; a second merge on that same worktree afterwards still runs rather than hitting the no-granted-worktree refusal; and the same case with uat APPROVED still cleans up normally. Assert too that the missing lane record still produces no red merge and no fabricated .bee/lanes/<feature>.json.
done_when: Under uat_stop close with an unapproved uat and no lane record on disk, --cleanup and worktree_cleanup_on_merge true no longer delete the worktree; the grant survives and a repeat merge still runs. The lane write stays best-effort and never fabricates a lane file or reddens the merge. The Merge and Off branches, and the approved-uat path, are unchanged. The worktree suite is green.
notes: Phase 4, fix-first on a judge observation against usp-2. Files are disjoint from usp-3's revision (uat.rs + close.rs) — the two run concurrently.

truths: Under uat_stop close with uat unapproved and NO lane record on disk, a merge passed --cleanup keeps the worktree, the branch, and the grant.
The same merge reports the cleanup suppression with the same result key usp-2 introduced.
A second merge on that worktree afterwards still runs instead of hitting the no-granted-worktree refusal.
With uat APPROVED, that same case cleans up normally.
A missing lane record still never reddens the merge and never causes a lane file to be fabricated.
The Merge and Off branches behave exactly as they did before this cell.

trace.outcome: merge_finish now computes uat_wait_set directly from the fail-closed precheck, so a missing lane record no longer lets cleanup tear down a worktree with a pending uat under uat_stop close.

report.outcome: merge_finish now computes uat_wait_set directly from the fail-closed precheck instead of reading it off the lane-write outcome, so a missing .bee/lanes/<feature>.json no longer lets --cleanup tear down a worktree with a pending uat under uat_stop close.
